findings.claim: The `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard around every new `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` is broader than needed. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` already exists in netstandard2.0 (via the System.Diagnostics.Tools contract) and in .NET Framework 4.0+. As a result, every consumer compiling for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework still gets formatters and resolvers with no attribute, which is a large share of MessagePack users. The requirement says all generated code is decorated; the derived criterion allows conditional emission only where the attribute does not exist. The same guard is repeated in EnumTemplate, UnionTemplate, StringKeyFormatterTemplate, ResolverTemplate and CompositeResolverTemplate.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageDownlevelTests.GeneratedFormattersCarryAttributeOnDownlevelTargets. It drives the generator with the NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK preprocessor symbol defined on the input and generated trees. It asserts that the generated MyObjectFormatter symbol has ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute, and it fails on head because the attribute is preprocessed away.
